decision: Log out clears the forward-auth cookie, then sends the browser to DAAX_AUTH_LOGOUT_URL exactly as configured (on the fleet https://auth.<host>.poley.dev/logout, Pocket ID's sign-out confirmation page). The browser stays on the IdP and does not return to daax; with the variable unset, Log out signs out of daax only and reloads.
rationale: Every host runs its own Pocket ID, so the logout target is per-host runtime configuration served in GET /api/auth/user, not a build-time NEXT_PUBLIC value. The previous default, auth.poley.dev's /api/oidc/end-session, was baked into every published image. Pocket ID's /logout frontend route takes no redirect parameter and goes to the IdP's own '/' after signing out.
alternatives: OIDC RP-initiated logout at <idp>/api/oidc/end-session with post_logout_redirect_uri would return the browser to daax. Rejected for now: Pocket ID only honours the redirect when it can resolve a client (client_id or id_token_hint) whose logout callback URLs include it, and daax holds neither, because Traefik forward-auth owns the OIDC session. Without one it falls back to <AppURL>/logout, the same confirmation page. Revisit if daax becomes an OIDC client itself.

decision: deploy/traefik-daax.yml.tpl defines no ForwardAuth of its own and gates daax, daax-ws and daax-code with edge-auth-required from the host's edge.yml (traefik-forward-auth on 127.0.0.1:4182 in front of this host's own Pocket ID). deploy-local.sh install-traefik-config refuses to install it unless deploy/host/check-edge-gate.sh accepts that edge.yml. The daax-host routers are removed until the host-local gate has an admins-only check.
rationale: The template still sent every login to 127.0.0.1:1411/api/forward-auth/verify, the retired shared IdP's fork, and that is the chain live on kinsale (Traefik API, 2026-11-15). Upstream Pocket ID has no /api/forward-auth/verify: it answers 404 on :1412 (v2.14.0) and :1413 (v2.19.2), and the edge.yml installed on kinsale still points edge-auth-required at it. The daax-host routers were admins-only through that fork's ?require_admin=true. traefik-forward-auth v4 has a conditions engine, but no admins-only condition has been verified against Pocket ID's claims, and a host shell behind any-signed-in-user would be a regression. The fleet's daax.yml has no daax-host route either.
alternatives: Keep pocket-id-auth pointed at the edge Pocket ID: rejected, upstream has no verify endpoint. Gate daax-host with edge-auth-required alone: rejected, it weakens a host-shell boundary. An unverified traefik-forward-auth ?if= condition: rejected until tested.

decision: This change keeps ForwardAuth header trust (dx#120 option 1) through the host's one shared Pocket ID and adds no OIDC relying-party mode. It reads traefik-forward-auth's X-Forwarded-Displayname as a display-name fallback. OIDC RP (option 2) stays a separate, owner-approved follow-up.
rationale: With #521 on main and the fleet edge's traefik-forward-auth in front of auth.<host>.poley.dev, daax depends on no shared IdP, and passkeys are host-local. On real Postgres, the first admin that identity-host.sh creates is an admin on their first request through that gate with no manual step, via the DAAX_ADMIN_USERS email/username pending grant (tests/integration/host-local-first-admin-pg.test.ts). What OIDC RP would add: the groups claim (traefik-forward-auth forwards none, so DAAX_GROUP_ROLE_MAP is inert), a session scoped to daax instead of every *.<host>.poley.dev app, no shared proxy secret, and RP-initiated logout back to daax. None of these blocks #120.
alternatives: daax as its own OIDC RP now: deferred to keep this PR to the gaps #120 needs, at the coordinator's direction. A separate Pocket ID for daax: rejected, a passkey binds to one origin, so every additional instance means one more enrolment per user per host.
